minutes.headline: Select Board heard FY21 budget updates and split over school five-year staffing request and debt; sewer seat filled.
minutes.summary: Three selectmen met jointly with the sewer commissioners to appoint a member, then took the town manager's report with updates affecting the FY21 budget. The board debated the five-year forecast, debt, the school staffing request, teacher contract negotiations, and an economic development committee. Formal action was limited to the sewer appointment, an ADA grant application, and adjournment.

what_happened.line: Selectmen and sewer commissioners voted jointly to appoint John Reynolds to the sewer commission until the next annual election.
The board heard FY21 budget updates: the health insurance and new growth estimates are to be reduced, and the assistant town mechanic position is eliminated in the preliminary budget.
Members objected to a school request to raise its budget substantially over five years, during a debate on the five-year forecast and debt, with no resolution.
A vote on supporting the MRPC technical assistance application for the ADA self-evaluation and transition plan was recorded, but the outcome was not audible.
A member asked to arrange an informal talk with the school committee on teacher contract negotiations; the economic development committee returns next week.

why_it_matters: The FY21 budget is still being shaped, and the school's five-year staffing request and the cost of the teacher contract bear on future tax bills.
Reduced revenue estimates and the loss of a town mechanic position change what the town budget, mostly taxes, can fund, while funds shift toward ADA compliance and facilities.
